title: Identification of Untreated Mean Trajectories in Randomized First-Passage Threshold Panels
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=incremental < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope; closest-literature-omitted@thm:donor-row-frontier and theorem-positioning-absent@prop:k3-segment-rigidity remain unrepaired.

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery extended the three-period benchmark to arbitrary finite pure-birth chains and horizons, with a donor-row frontier, recursive joint mean image, and full-law sharpness. The independent math referee found no proof defect, but the cold novelty review graded the delivered population-identification result incremental against the field floor. Boundary-valid joint inference would require a new inferential project; two literature and positioning findings also remain unresolved.
tldr: The field-level result is an arbitrary-finite-chain theorem for prospectively observed randomized first-passage panels: it identifies exactly which pure-birth rows are learned from the chosen threshold-arm support, recursively characterizes the full joint untreated-mean trajectory across all horizons with explicit upstream-zero and excess-horizon clauses, and proves sharp attainment relative to a fixed observed law while fixing conditional outcome channels only on positive-probability stopped words. Randomized transfusion-trigger protocols motivate the design class: Murphy et al. document that TITRe2 randomized restrictive versus liberal hemoglobin-trigger thresholds, and, after reversing or scaling an ordered severity state, the benchmark asks whether an added threshold arm covers a previously unidentified reachable row and whether a reported multi-horizon effect vector is jointly feasible rather than only horizon by horizon. Full-law sharpness establishes that the joint set cannot be narrowed from the retained stopped-path law and positive-cell post-initiation channels alone. This is a benchmark and design implication, not an analysis of TITRe2, a transport result, or a general clinical recommendation. The supporting stopped-panel experiment is indexed by \((p,\gamma)\), the \(K=T=3\) singular image is a worked corollary, and the \(23/375\) calculation is only an ad hoc implementation diagnostic.
gap: Han identifies dynamic-treatment quantities in a distinct endogenous-treatment model using period-specific exclusion restrictions together with a behavioral and information assumption, and Alvarez and Ferrando give sharp bounds built from locally feasible dynamic kernels. Han discusses rank invariance as a condition from Vytlacil and Yildiz rather than maintaining it. Neither result states, for a prospectively observed randomized threshold protocol, the exact donor-threshold row frontier, the zero-product recursive joint image, or fixed-observed-law attainment needed to decide whether another threshold arm learns a reachable row and whether a multi-horizon vector is jointly compatible.
fill: The linked arbitrary-\((K,T)\) theorem certifies which reachable untreated rows an added threshold arm would cover, tests joint rather than horizon-wise feasibility of untreated mean and effect vectors, and proves that the resulting joint set cannot be narrowed from the retained stopped-path law and positive-cell post-initiation channels alone. The exact \((p,\gamma)\)-indexed experiment supplies supporting machinery, and the result is a benchmark and design implication rather than a TITRe2 analysis, transport result, or clinical recommendation.
